executive_summary: EUR/USD trades at 1.15503 (5 August close), up 1.13% over one month but down 0.93% over three months, up 0.24% over six and flat (-0.09%) over twelve — a pair that has absorbed a war, an energy shock, a first ECB hike since 2023 and a change of Federal Reserve Chair without going anywhere in index terms. The pair sits at the 31st percentile of its 52-week range (1.13239–1.20656), having based at the 24 June low and broken decisively above 1.1500 on 29–31 July before consolidating in a tight 1.1502–1.1560 band. The dominant bilateral narrative is symmetric hawkishness colliding with asymmetric energy exposure: futures price roughly 90% odds of an ECB hike on 10 September against 77% for the Fed on 16 September, so the 137.5bp policy gap is not compressing in the way most 2026 euro forecasts assume, while the same barrel of Brent that taxes the euro area now pays a net-energy-exporting United States. The differential that neither standalone dossier fully prices is that this makes EUR/USD the highest-beta negative-oil pair in the G10 — and that the live Hormuz de-escalation headlines of early August have therefore flipped the terms-of-trade channel from a euro-negative into a pair-positive within days of both dossiers' valuation date. Positioning is the second bilateral amplifier: leveraged funds are simultaneously short EUR futures (-65,198 contracts, a sample extreme) and long the USD Index (+17,197), so the crowded trade is short EUR/USD, while asset managers hold a +209,326-contract EUR long that is the mirror-image strategic overhang. We are tactically Bullish EUR/USD at conviction 2 (weighted score +0.2302, target 1.1620) on the data-momentum differential, the positioning squeeze and the American term-premium repricing, and strategically Bullish at conviction 2 (+0.1122, six-month target 1.1680) — a deliberately weak strategic call because the euro area's winter gas balance and the 17 November French budget vote sit directly against a modest, ECB-driven differential compression. The caveat that caps conviction: the pair is 1.5% above relative-REER fair value at 1.1363, carry costs 137.5bp a year against a long, and the options market's 25-delta skew still pays a premium for euro puts.

market_context.valuation_assessment: On relative real-effective terms both dossiers agree: the euro area's REER sits +0.5% above its 30-month mean against the United States' -1.0%, implying the euro is roughly 1.5% rich versus the dollar and a relative-REER fair value of 1.1363. Spot at 1.15503 is therefore about 190 pips above that anchor — a small overvaluation, well inside noise, and the two dossiers' independent derivations reconcile to the same number. The BIS real broad REERs are 102.69 for the euro area and 107.84 for the United States, both within roughly one percent of their own means, so neither leg of this pair is the cheap or the expensive currency in the G10. Valuation is dormant as an independent driver: it neither supports nor vetoes a directional view, and its only useful output is that it removes the structurally overvalued dollar mean-reversion tailwind. Range percentile (31) is the more informative positional statistic than valuation here.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The ECB deposit facility rate is 2.25% against a Fed funds midpoint of 3.625%, so a long EUR/USD position pays -137.5bp annualised — the euro has been the funding leg for three years. Against 5.25 three-month implied volatility, the carry-to-vol ratio is -0.26, meaning a long surrenders roughly a quarter of one standard deviation of annual price movement to financing, material at six months and near-irrelevant at four weeks. Market forward points of +14.2/+42.2/+86.3 pips at 1M/3M/6M give outrights of 1.15645/1.15925/1.16366, with the 6M points exceeding the pure carry differential due to cross-currency basis. The carry regime is working, and it is working against this pair: over twelve months the euro has gained only against the two currencies it out-yields (JPY, CHF) while the dollar has held its ground against everything it out-yields. The critical bilateral observation is that carry alone cannot beat this pair higher — a long EUR/USD is a spot trade that has to overcome financing, which is why the tactical view is time-boxed and the strategic view is expressed against the forward curve rather than spot.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The differential is 137.5bp against the euro and, critically for a four-week view, it is not moving. Futures put the odds of the ECB and the Fed raising rates in September at 90% and 77% respectively, with the probability of two hikes in 2026 at 60% and 56% — the ECB is expected to make the first move. If both deliver 25bp, the differential is exactly 137.5bp on 17 September — no compression, no carry relief, no pair signal. The pricing is consistent with spot: at 1.15503 the pair is 190 pips above relative-REER fair value and the 6M forward at 1.16366 embeds only the mechanical 1.5% annualised carry-unwind. The transmission channel is the UST-Bund spread, which has a documented -0.5 to -0.7 correlation with this pair and sat at 152–159bp on 29–31 July after both legs rose 26–27bp in July — the spread has been dormant for a month despite two hawkish central banks offsetting each other exactly. The one live asymmetry inside the window is sequencing: the ECB meets 10 September, six days before the FOMC, so the euro leg sets the tone and a delivered ECB hike into an unresolved Fed is mechanically pair-positive for a week. That is not enough to overcome a fully priced curve, and Neutral is the honest reading.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the differential does compress, modestly, and the compression comes from the euro leg. Markets now fully price the ECB deposit rate reaching 2.75% by early 2027, i.e. two more hikes, against a Fed whose June SEP median of 3.8% for end-2026 implies at most one and whose 2027 median of 3.6% embeds a cut. Deliver 50bp from the ECB and 25bp from the Fed and the gap narrows to 112.5bp; deliver 50bp and nothing and it narrows to 87.5bp — a 25–50bp compression worth roughly 0.8–2.0 big figures on this pair at its historical beta to the UST-Bund spread. The deeper bilateral argument is real rates: the euro area's 2.25% policy rate against 2.9% July HICP is a real rate of -0.65%, while the United States at 3.625% against 3.5% CPI is +0.13% — the ECB is further behind its own inflation than the Fed is behind its own, giving it more runway. The counterweight is that the Fed's own hawkish minority is real (three sitting dissenters for a hike) and that the 2027 dots the market is trading are the least credible element of the projection set, so the compression is contingent rather than mechanical. This is the single largest positive contributor to the strategic score and it is deliberately held at 52 confidence, because a 25–50bp narrowing against a 137.5bp starting deficit is an improvement in the rate of decline of the carry drag, not its removal.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The data-momentum differential is the cleanest bullish signal in this report, because the two economies surprised in opposite directions in July. Euro-area Q2 GDP beat at +0.4% q/q against a 0.2% consensus (roughly 1.6% annualised), the July flash composite PMI rose to a five-month high of 51.9 from 50.0, ifo climbed a third consecutive month to 86.6, ZEW German expectations leapt 15.8 points to +26.3 against an 18.0 consensus, and flash HICP accelerated on all four measures that matter (headline 2.9%, core 2.5%, services 3.3%, energy 10.0%). The United States delivered the mirror image: Q2 GDP at 1.5% annualised versus 2.1% in Q1, June payrolls of just 57,000 with 74,000 of downward back revisions, participation down 0.3pp to 61.5%, and Conference Board confidence at 90.8. The transatlantic growth premium that underwrote the dollar for three years has closed on the latest prints — 1.6% annualised versus 1.5%. The transmission is direct and asymmetric: with the ECB's September decision hinging on the 1 September flash HICP and the Fed's on the 7 August payroll report and 12 August CPI, European surprises currently push the pair up through rate expectations while American surprises are more likely to push it up through growth disappointment. The offsetting risk inside the window is that July's US CPI mechanically re-accelerates on the energy reversal, which is pair-negative — but with core CPI at 2.6% and the Dallas Fed trimmed mean at 2.2%, a headline-only re-acceleration is a thinner dollar signal than it looks.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At one to six months the inflation impulse on both sides is self-liquidating and the two economies converge, so the factor loses its directional content. Euro-area inflation ex-energy is 2.2% and unchanged, food inflation has decelerated to 1.2%, the ECB wage tracker sits at 2.3% for 2026 with no second-round effects visible, and the ECB's own projections take HICP from a 3.4% Q3–Q4 peak to 2.3% in 2027 — an energy shock without a wage response drops out of the year-on-year comparison by construction. The American picture is structurally identical: the Dallas Fed trimmed mean at 2.2% and core CPI at 2.6% both sit near target while core PCE at 3.3% is being generated by a narrow set of components, and the Fed's own SEP takes headline PCE to 2.3% in 2027 and 2.0% in 2028. On growth, the official forecasts still separate them (ECB 0.8% for 2026 versus a 2.2% SEP median) and if that gap reasserts itself it is pair-negative; if the Q2 convergence persists it is pair-positive. Both economies are net energy importers of the same shock in inflation terms even though only one is a net exporter in trade terms, which means the inflation channel is far more symmetric for this pair than for, say, EUR/NOK. Genuine Neutral: the impulses are the same shape, the same size and on the same timetable.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: EUR/USD is a low-beta risk pair under the framework's classification, and the current regime confirms it: the STOXX Europe 600 set a record 655.45 on 31 July and the S&P 500 a record 7,489.72, the VIX is 17.09, US IG spreads are 80–81bp and high yield 281–284bp — and the pair moved only 1.13% in the month. The euro's documented correlation to the Euro Stoxx 50 is +0.2 to +0.4, the loosest of its cross-asset relationships, so a record European equity market delivers very little currency. What does move this pair is position on the dollar smile: the euro is 57.6% of the DXY and is the mechanical anti-dollar, so a benign, liquid, non-stressed global regime in which safe-haven dollar demand fades is the middle of the smile where EUR/USD does best. That is exactly where we are, and the incremental bullish input is energy diplomacy: the euro has traded slightly above $1.15 near its highest level since 16 June as easing geopolitical tensions improved risk sentiment and oil prices tumbled on optimism that diplomacy could end the US-Iran conflict. The offsetting mechanism is that the euro at 2.25% is itself a funding currency in a low-vol risk-on regime, which mechanically finances euro-funded carry trades and sells euros — the leveraged short of 65,198 contracts built during a record equity month is the evidence. Net: the risk channel is mildly pair-positive because the anti-dollar effect currently outweighs the funding-currency drag, but the weight is low and the confidence modest.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk channel becomes symmetric for this pair and therefore contributes nothing. The escalation branch is unambiguously pair-negative and doubly so: a Hormuz re-closure hits European energy supply lines directly while delivering the United States a simultaneous safe-haven bid and a terms-of-trade gain as a net energy exporter, an asymmetry the base-currency dossier estimates at -2.5% to -4% on EUR/USD and the quote-currency dossier at +3–5% on the DXY. The de-escalation branch is equally pair-positive by the same mechanism reversed. Both branches are live, neither is clearly more likely inside six months, and the framework's low weight for this pair correctly reflects that the beta to generic risk appetite is small while the beta to this specific geopolitical binary is large — which is why we book the geopolitical content in Factors 5 and 7 rather than here. What remains in Factor 3 is the euro's funding-currency drag against the dollar's smile position, and those two roughly cancel over months. tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the factor where the bilateral read is strictly stronger than either standalone view, because the two legs of the speculative position reinforce rather than offset. Leveraged funds were net short 65,198 EUR futures on the 28 July CFTC report — an extension of the 56,671-contract short that was already the 0th percentile of a 25-week sample — while ICE US Dollar Index Non-Commercials were net long 17,197 contracts and added 1,583 in the same week. Read separately, each dossier calls its own leg crowded; read together, the crowded trade is short EUR/USD, and it was being added to on 28 July, three sessions before the pair broke 1.1500 and two before the DXY lost 100. That timing is the entire tactical case: the CFTC snapshot predates a 1.5% adverse move, so the reported position is already marked against and the marginal speculative seller is exhausted. Position size matters for squeeze mechanics — 65,198 contracts is roughly $9.4bn notional inside an 819,806-lot contract, the deepest CME FX market, so a forced cover has depth to run through. The bilateral flow overlay is the hedge-ratio channel and it points the same way: Danish institutional investors, representing around 9% of EU pension and insurance assets, raised their hedge ratio on dollar assets from roughly 60% in January 2025 to over 70% by December 2025, and the February 2026 reading of 70.3% is actually the lowest since before Liberation Day. Morgan Stanley has quantified the potential: a drop in hedging costs would drive flows of more than $200 billion and prop up the euro. Against all this, asset managers hold +209,326 EUR contracts long, which is real and is the reason confidence is 63 rather than 80.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a strategic horizon the fast-money extreme has by definition resolved and the structural flow data takes over, and that data currently favours the dollar. The IMF's COFER release shows the dollar's share of world reserves rising to 57.13% in 2026Q1 from 56.42%, while the euro's fell to 20.03% from 20.38% — a second consecutive quarterly decline for the euro and a direct falsification of the de-dollarisation premise that underpins most strategic EUR/USD bull cases. US Treasury TIC data recorded $262.8bn of net foreign purchases of long-term US securities in May against a $226.8bn quarterly current-account deficit, so the American external position is being financed with a large margin. The relevant crowded position at this horizon is the asset-manager EUR long of 209,326 contracts, which has been reducing at roughly 20,000–26,000 contracts a month and would continue to reduce if the euro-area recovery stalls into Q4 — persistent supply rather than a violent unwind, and a standing cap on rallies. The genuine offset is the hedge-ratio channel: the ECB has flagged that euro-area investors may shift toward lower dollar allocations and increased currency hedging with a greater euro home bias, with some signs of a step-up in demand for euro-denominated assets during 2025. ING's assessment is more cautious, and the February data went the other way. On balance the observable structural flows are pair-negative and the hedge-ratio channel is a forecast, so we take a mild Bearish stance at 50 confidence rather than a Neutral.

The ECB has published an explicit reaction function, longer-term inflation expectations are anchored at around 2%, and the June hike was carried unanimously under every scenario in its own projection set. The Federal Reserve's hawkish framework is newer and thinner: Chair Warsh has been in post since 22 May, the framework rests on a single Chair's stated intolerance for elevated inflation rather than on a track record, the 2027 SEP median of 3.6% embeds cuts that sit awkwardly with the rhetoric, and the Fed's institutional independence is under live legal challenge, with the Supreme Court having blocked the removal of Governor Cook only on narrow procedural grounds while the merits remain in the lower courts. tactical.bilateral_analysis: For a pair in which the dollar is the quote currency and the euro is 57.6% of the DXY, this factor transmits directly rather than through a vehicle-currency channel, and right now it is dollar-supportive. Domestic dollar liquidity has become genuinely scarce: reserve balances fell to $2,944,541mn on 29 July, down $355bn year-on-year, the overnight reverse repo facility is drained to roughly $2bn so there is no buffer between Treasury cash operations and bank reserves, the Treasury General Account is at $997.9bn, and SOFR printed 3.65% exactly at the interest rate on reserve balances with a 75th percentile of 3.70%. Repo clearing at the top of the corridor on $3,011bn of volume is a marginal-cost signal, and a rising marginal cost of dollar funding pushes the pair down. On the euro side, the Eurosystem's own balance sheet is contracting at roughly €5bn a week with APP running off at ~€26bn a month and PEPP at ~€13.6bn, and TLTRO III has been fully matured since December 2024 — so both central banks are draining, but the American drain is concentrated in a single reserve number close to the Committee's own comfort floor. The critical caveat, and it is a hard gap in both dossiers, is that the 3-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis was not retrievable from any source this cycle, so the assessment rests on SOFR-IORB (0bp), central bank liquidity swaps outstanding ($132mn) and standing repo usage ($3mn), all of which say there is no offshore stress. Bearish for the pair at only 50 confidence because the direct measure is missing and because the credit market corroborates abundance rather than scarcity.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the American liquidity picture inverts and becomes pair-positive, because the Federal Reserve has already announced the policy that resolves the scarcity. Quantitative tightening is over: the 29 July directive instructs the Desk to purchase Treasury bills to maintain an ample level of reserves and to reinvest all principal from Treasury and agency holdings, so the effective pace of runoff is zero and total assets have grown to $6,738,190mn from $6,646,340mn in March. The structural dollar scarcity that supported the currency through 2024–25 has been removed, and because the euro is 57.6% of the DXY it absorbs the largest single share of any resulting dollar decline. Meanwhile the Eurosystem is still passively tightening at ~€5bn a week, which reinforces the ECB's hiking cycle at the margin and is euro-supportive. Two qualifications hold confidence to 52. First, seasonality: the 31 December year-end dollar funding turn falls inside the horizon and reliably widens cross-currency basis, a temporary pair negative. Second, the euro at 2.25% is itself a cheap funding currency, and abundant dollar liquidity plus 5% volatility is precisely the regime in which euro-funded carry trades proliferate and mechanically sell euros — the 65,198-contract leveraged short built in exactly that regime is the evidence. Our view is that a second ECB hike is the point at which the euro's funding-currency status begins to erode and the channel flips fully in the pair's favour, and that is not priced as a EUR/USD event at all.

That data cluster arrived into a speculative community that is simultaneously short 65,198 EUR contracts and long 17,197 USD Index contracts — the crowded trade is short EUR/USD, and it was added to on 28 July, three sessions before the pair broke 1.1500. Better euro data raises September ECB pricing, which raises the cost of the short, which forces covering in an 819,806-lot contract; weaker American data does the same from the other side. The base and quote dossier views therefore conflict on the surface (both tactically bullish their own currency) and reconcile bilaterally in the euro's favour, because the euro's bullish drivers are pair-specific (data momentum, positioning) while the dollar's are largely index-wide or already priced. The genuinely bilateral modifier is Factor 5: both dossiers computed the terms-of-trade channel at Brent $91.82 on 1 August and reached opposite standalone conclusions that netted to a strongly bearish pair, but oil has since tumbled on optimism that diplomacy could end the US-Iran conflict, with the US Treasury Secretary saying a Hormuz reopening deal could be reached within days — and because the euro area imports the energy while the United States now exports it, a de-escalation is doubly pair-positive. What is priced versus what we expect: spot at 1.15503 prices a pair that fails again at 1.1550, with the options market still paying a premium for euro puts (25-delta RR -0.25) and CFTC data lagging four business days behind a market that has already moved 1.5%; we expect the pair to hold the breakout and grind into the 1.1598–1.1621 cluster. The path of least resistance is up, because the marginal speculative seller is exhausted and the marginal buyer has four dated catalysts to work with: the 7 August payroll report, the 27 August ECB Account, the 1 September flash HICP and the 10 September ECB decision with staff projections in Berlin — the last of which lands six days before the FOMC, so the euro leg sets the September tone. The conviction drivers are that both the data differential and the positioning extreme are observed rather than forecast, and that the invalidation level at 1.1470 is close, unambiguous and structurally meaningful. The conviction limiters are equally concrete: negative carry of 137.5bp, a declining 200-day at 1.16214 sitting inside our own target zone, and a Factor 5 bullish flip that rests on a diplomatic outcome we cannot underwrite.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.1122 is barely above the Neutral boundary and is less than half the tactical +0.2302. The arithmetic is a near-standoff: three positives totalling +0.2600 (Policy & Rates +0.1352, Guidance +0.0624, USD Liquidity +0.0624) against three negatives totalling -0.1478 (External Balance -0.0928, Flows -0.0300, Event Risk -0.0250), with four factors contributing exactly zero. External Balance alone offsets 69% of the Policy & Rates contribution, and that is the central strategic tension in this pair: the differential compression that lifts EUR/USD is caused by an ECB hiking into an energy shock that simultaneously erodes the euro's external account and pays the American one. The rate benefit and the terms-of-trade cost share a single cause and very nearly cancel.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the pair is dominated by Policy & Rates at 0.26 and External Balance at 0.16, which together carry 42% of the score and point in opposite directions with almost equal force. Policy & Rates turns Bullish because the differential trajectory finally favours the pair: markets fully price the ECB deposit rate reaching 2.75% by early 2027 against a Fed whose SEP median implies at most one hike and whose 2027 median embeds a cut, so a 137.5bp gap compresses to 112.5bp or 87.5bp — worth 0.8 to 2.0 big figures at the pair's historical beta to the UST-Bund spread. The euro area's real policy rate of -0.65% against the United States' +0.13% says the ECB has further to travel than the Fed does, and Guidance reinforces this at a 0.12 weight through a credibility differential that favours the euro: an ECB with a published reaction function and anchored expectations against a ten-week-old Fed chairmanship whose framework is untested and whose institutional independence is under live litigation. USD Liquidity adds a third leg, because QT has ended, the Fed's balance sheet is growing again, and the euro's 57.6% DXY weight makes it the mechanical recipient of any resulting dollar decline. Against that stands the single most serious structural problem this pair has, and it is bilateral rather than euro-specific: the euro area is a large net energy importer entering winter with storage at 49–55% (roughly 10 percentage points behind), a balance-of-summer TTF contract trading €2.68/MWh over Winter 26/27, a self-imposed Russian LNG ban landing at end-2026 and a current-account surplus already down from 2.0% to 1.7% of GDP — while the United States earns a $63.61 Gulf Coast crack spread and finances a 2.9%-of-GDP deficit with $262.8bn of monthly portfolio inflows. Under the framework's direction rules, oil ↑ is −EUR / ++USD and gas ↑ is −−EUR / +USD, making EUR/USD the most oil-negative major pair in the G10. Event Risk and Flows compound the negative modestly: the 17 November French PLF vote is a 20–25% censure-and-dissolution binary that transmits through the OAT-Bund spread, while COFER shows the dollar's reserve share rising to 57.13% as the euro's fell to 20.03%. Notably, the twin fiscal deteriorations cancel: both sovereigns are getting worse, the American one is already being repriced in a 5.27% 30-year and the French one is not priced at all, so Factor 8 nets to zero — an observation available only bilaterally. What is priced versus what we expect: the consensus cluster for end-2026 sits at 1.18–1.25 with a named median near 1.20, built on Fed cuts that the 29 July FOMC's three hike-dissents make unlikely; the six-month forward is 1.16366; we expect 1.1680, which is 43 pips above the forward and roughly 320 pips below consensus. The path of least resistance is sideways with a widening distribution, and the dated catalysts that decide it are 10 September, 16 September, the shared 30 September date, 17 November, 9 and 17 December and end-December. The conviction driver is not direction but the identification of a genuine offsetting structure — this is a marginal Bullish we have argued for, not defaulted to — and the honest conclusion is that with a base-case edge of only 43 pips against the forward, the strategic expression is long volatility and relative value rather than a directional spot position.

Long EUR/CAD is second on the zero-carry-to-positive-carry swing. EUR/USD ranks behind both and behind long EUR/JPY on carry-to-vol, ahead only of the euro's expressions against the energy and commodity bloc. Among short-dollar expressions, USD/NOK short, AUD/USD long, NZD/USD long and USD/SGD short all screen better. The critical cross-check: the standalone dossiers rank EUR 6th and USD 4th strategically, which on a naive subtraction implies a bearish EUR/USD. Our bilateral analysis reaches a marginally bullish conclusion for three specific reasons — the energy shock nets less one-sidedly than either dossier assumes standalone, the twin fiscal deteriorations cancel rather than accumulating against the euro, and the ECB's larger hiking runway from a -0.65% real policy rate, delivered at meetings that precede the FOMC at both the September and December turns, is a pair-specific sequencing advantage invisible in either standalone ranking. That divergence from the naive subtraction is precisely why conviction is 2 and not 3.

First, the transmission assumption is wrong: almost every forecast in the 1.20–1.25 cluster is built on Fed cuts, yet the 29 July FOMC held 9–3 with all three dissents favouring a hike and the June SEP median for end-2026 is 3.8% against a 3.625% midpoint — compression will come from the euro leg alone, roughly halving its magnitude. Second, the consensus does not net the energy shock bilaterally, reading the ECB's hiking cycle as a euro positive without pricing that the same shock has taken the euro-area current-account surplus from 2.0% to 1.7% of GDP while paying a net-energy-exporting United States a $63.61 crack spread — the rate benefit and the terms-of-trade cost share one cause and largely cancel. Third, the consensus has not dated the French binary: the 17 November PLF 2027 solemn vote is invisible in the OAT forward curve and EUR/USD option expiries, yet EUR/USD continues to take its cue from the OAT-Bund yield spread and a move through 100bp historically drags the pair 1.0–1.5% lower independent of the ECB.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: Selling a six-month EUR/USD forward at 1.16366 against an expected 1.1680 earns only +43 pips, which is honest for conviction 2; being long the pair tactically from 1.15503 into a 1.1620 target earns approximately 117 pips against a crowd positioned the other way; being long three-to-six-month volatility at 5.25–5.46 implied earns on realisation regardless of direction, because the November–December calendar carries no premium at all.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If the consensus is right and EUR/USD reaches 1.20 by year-end, a strategic position anchored on 1.1680 misses 320 pips of appreciation, and the specific mechanism that would make consensus right is a Hormuz settlement plus a US labour-market break that converts the FOMC's hawkish dissenters into a cutting majority. We assign that combination roughly 25%, exactly the weight on our strategic upside case, and a long-volatility expression profits in that scenario too.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: Aligned — both horizons are Bullish EUR/USD at conviction 2, with the tactical score roughly double the strategic. The thesis is directionally consistent but decays sharply with time, the inverse of the usual carry-driven pattern. The decay is driven almost entirely by weight migration: Inflation & Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and Flows & Positioning from 0.10 to 0.06 — the two factors contributing +0.1152 and +0.0630 tactically — while External Balance rises from 0.09 to 0.16 and flips sign from Bullish to Bearish, a swing of -0.1396 in contribution. Policy & Rates switches from Neutral to Bullish and adds +0.1352, which partly compensates but not enough. Substantively, the tactical case rests on two things with short half-lives — a July data cluster and a reinforcing two-cohort speculative short — while the strategic case must contend with a European winter gas balance and a French budget calendar that only get heavier with time.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Mid-to-late September 2026, specifically the window between the 10 September ECB decision in Berlin and the shared 30 September date on which the French PLF 2027 goes to the Conseil des ministres and US fiscal-2026 appropriations lapse.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Because the horizons agree in direction, a single position does not need to be flipped mid-horizon, materially improving after-cost economics against a 137.5bp carry drag. But because the strength decays by half, the position must be sized down rather than held flat: the tactical long should be sized for a two-to-four-week hold with a hard invalidation at 1.1470 and reduced into rather than held through the 10 September decision. The strategic view is not a spot view at all — with an expected value of +3 pips against the forward — and the exploitable strategic position is long three-to-six-month volatility. In relative-value terms, long EUR/CHF works on both horizons while long EUR/USD works cleanly on only one.

catalysts.rationale: The single largest tactical risk in this analysis and the only event with a visible option premium (1-week implied 6.13 versus 1-month 4.99). June added just 57,000 with 74,000 of downward revisions and participation at 61.5%, so a print below 25,000 would break the dollar's growth leg into a freshly added speculative long with no positioning cushion beneath it, and the pair should clear 1.1600. A print above 100,000 with wage growth above 4% validates the FOMC's three hike-dissenters, re-widens the UST-Bund spread through 165bp and sends the pair back to 1.1470.

catalysts.event: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (first edition incorporating the July escalation)
catalysts.rationale: The July STEO was released on 7 July, before the ceasefire breach, and forecasts Brent averaging $74 in Q3 2026 and $65 in 2027 against a spot near $92. Because the euro area imports the energy and the United States exports it, the revision direction moves the pair with roughly a ∓1.0% response per ±10% Brent — a downward revision on Hormuz reopening optimism is bullish the pair; an upward revision confirming constrained transit through end-2026 is bearish.

The most important scheduled repricing event of the month and the clearest bearish-pair item in August. June's headline fell 0.4% m/m entirely because energy dropped 5.7% during the brief post-ceasefire oil collapse, and Brent has since traded from $86.99 to $105.32 and back to $91.82. The energy component mechanically reverses, and a headline at or above 3.8% would put a September Fed hike alongside the September ECB hike, freezing the differential at 137.5bp. The mitigant is compositional: core CPI at 2.6% and the trimmed mean at 2.2% mean a headline-only re-acceleration is a thinner dollar signal than it appears.

catalysts.event: Expiry of the 60-day no-charge Hormuz transit window under the US-Iran memorandum
catalysts.rationale: The memorandum granted safe passage with no charge for 60 days from 17 June, so the window lapses around 16 August. Because the euro area is a large net energy importer and the United States a net exporter, escalation delivers the dollar a haven bid and a terms-of-trade gain while hitting the euro's import bill — a double negative for the pair estimated at -2.5% to -4%. De-escalation is the mirror image, and the current momentum favours it: the US Treasury Secretary has said a deal to reopen the Strait could be reached within days, with Qatar reporting mediator progress.

catalysts.event: Minutes of the 28-29 July FOMC meeting
catalysts.rationale: The minutes will reveal how close the Committee came to hiking, given three dissents for a 25bp increase against a unanimous 12-0 hold only six weeks earlier and a June record showing that many participants saw the appropriate end-2026 rate above the current range. A hawkish internal distribution would push Fed September pricing from 77% toward 90%, equalising the two central banks and removing the pair's rate-trajectory case.

catalysts.event: Publication of the ECB Account of the 23 July 2026 meeting
catalysts.rationale: Lagarde disclosed at the July press conference that some governors asked whether a hike should be considered; the Account will document how many and how forcefully. Given that the June Account recorded a unanimous hike and an all-member view that inflation risks are to the upside, a hawkish July Account would push ECB September pricing from around 90% toward certainty and re-price the depo path beyond 2.75%, forcing further covering of the 65,198-contract leveraged EUR short.

Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole, and the surprise direction is hawkish because the market has softened its Fed tightening expectations since the June payroll miss. He has used every prior venue to reinforce the 2% commitment and has openly questioned how much accommodation the balance sheet is providing — a live topic in a year when reserves have fallen $355bn. Any signal that September is on the table equalises the two September meetings and is pair-negative.

catalysts.event: Fitch scheduled sovereign rating review of France
catalysts.rationale: Fitch downgraded France to A+ in September 2025 and carries a Stable outlook. With the 2025 deficit at 5.1% of GDP, debt at 117.5% and a Bercy-commissioned report warning of 5.9% in 2027, an outlook change to Negative is live ahead of the PLF 2027 process and would take OAT-Bund from 82bp toward 95–100bp. That matters for this pair specifically because EUR/USD continues to take its cue from the OAT-Bund spread.

The decisive input for the 10 September ECB decision. July printed 2.9% headline, 2.5% core, 3.3% services and 10.0% energy, all accelerating. A print at or above 2.9% locks in the September hike and sustains market pricing of a 2.75% deposit rate by early 2027; a print at or below 2.6% cuts hike odds below 60% and invalidates the tactical thesis outright.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision plus ECB staff projections (Bundesbank, Berlin)
catalysts.rationale: The single most important dated event for this pair, and it lands six days before the FOMC, so the euro leg sets the September tone. A 25bp hike to 2.50% is roughly 90% priced, so the rate itself is a sell-the-fact; the projections carry the larger information content, because an upward revision to 2026 HICP toward 3.2% with 2027 held at or above 2.3% forces the curve toward the 2.75% terminal, while a downward 2027 revision caps the cycle and removes the pair's strategic Policy & Rates support.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision plus Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The dollar leg of the differential, and the second half of a two-stage September event structure. Futures put Fed September hike odds at 77% against 90% for the ECB, so the market expects parallel tightening; if the Fed delivers, the 137.5bp gap survives intact and the pair's entire strategic Policy & Rates contribution is halved. The SEP's 2027 median of 3.6% is the item to watch — an upward revision toward the 2026 median is the most pair-negative outcome available.

catalysts.event: French PLF 2027 to Conseil des ministres AND expiry of US fiscal-2026 appropriations
catalysts.rationale: The densest bilateral date in the horizon and a genuine two-sided fiscal event. The French budget process opens with ministry spending growth capped at 0.4% while debt interest rises €12.3bn, and the 2026 budget required Article 49.3 to pass. Simultaneously US federal appropriations lapse, and 2026 has already produced a partial DHS shutdown from 14 February to 30 April, so the base rate for disruption is empirically high. Two fiscal negatives landing on one date is the clearest illustration that this pair has no fiscal safe haven.

All 435 House seats and a third of the Senate determine fiscal and trade policy for the remainder of the presidential term. Because judicial rulings have already voided the IEEPA tariff architecture and left roughly $166bn of refunds in dispute, congressional control has unusually direct implications for the revenue path underpinning the term premium currently sitting in a 5.27% 30-year — and it is that term premium, not the policy rate, that made the dollar fall in July despite a 37bp rise in the 10-year.

catalysts.event: French Assemblée nationale solemn vote on the PLF 2027 as a whole
catalysts.rationale: The peak risk date of the European autumn and the largest unpriced binary in this pair. If Article 49.3 is used without a pre-negotiated compromise, a censure motion follows; a successful censure means dissolution and snap legislative elections weeks before a presidential campaign, taking OAT-Bund from 82bp toward 130bp. Estimated at 20–25%. The bilateral transmission is documented: EUR/USD takes its cue from the OAT-Bund spread, and a move through 100bp has historically dragged the pair 1.0–1.5% lower independent of the ECB.

catalysts.event: Full EU ban on Russian LNG imports takes effect
catalysts.rationale: A self-imposed supply cut landing in the same month as constrained Hormuz transit and EU storage that entered winter roughly 10 percentage points behind, with Kpler's base case revising global LNG exports down 21Mt for July 2026 to March 2027. Under the framework's direction rules JKM up is −−EUR and, for the world's largest LNG exporter, +USD — the most one-sided calendar item in the horizon for the pair, landing precisely when European heating demand peaks.

invalidators.mechanism: 1.1470 is the base of the 29–31 July breakout and the level at which the reclaimed 100-day (1.15397) and the flipped 1.1499 pivot both fail. The breakout holding while shorts cover is the whole tactical mechanism, so the structural and flow invalidations are the same level and the 65,198-contract short would stop covering and re-build.

invalidators.mechanism: The entire strategic Policy & Rates contribution (+0.1352, 55% of the gross positive strategic score) rests on the differential compressing by 25–50bp from the euro leg. Parallel tightening is a bilateral outcome invisible in either standalone dossier and would take the strategic score from +0.1122 to -0.0230.

invalidators.mechanism: A move from 152–159bp through 130bp is 22–29bp of compression, worth roughly 0.8–1.0 big figures on this pair at its documented -0.5 to -0.7 correlation, and would confirm the euro leg is doing the work rather than requiring Fed cuts. invalidators.mechanism: This resolves the single largest strategic negative in this analysis in the pair's favour: the euro area's import bill collapses, the euro-area current-account surplus recovers toward 2.0%+ of GDP, and the United States simultaneously loses its terms-of-trade gain and its haven premium. It is one of only two spreads a major bank names as driving the pair, and it currently trades through Italy — an inversion of the euro area's historic credit hierarchy.

assumptions: Spot and price-derived metrics: all price-derived figures (spot 1.15503 at the 5 August close, 1M/3M/6M/1Y performance, 52-week range and percentile, 50/100/200-day SMAs, trend regime, recent price-action narrative) are taken exclusively from the provided Twelve Data daily OHLC series (390 observations, 9 June 2025 to 5 August 2026). There is a four-day gap between the stated valuation date (1 August 2026) and the latest close (5 August); the two dossiers were constructed at a 1 August snapshot with EUR/USD at 1.15335, a 17-pip difference. The four extra sessions contain the early-August Hormuz de-escalation headlines that flip Factor 5's tactical stance relative to both dossiers, disclosed explicitly rather than smoothed over.

Realised volatility: the 20-day realised volatility figure of approximately 4.4% annualised is computed from close-to-close returns in the provided OHLC series, annualised at √252. It is consistent with but not identical to the quote-currency dossier's 4.22% reading dated 31 July.

Volatility surface and skew: all implied volatilities and risk reversals are carried from the quote-currency dossier, sourced from a single dealer's OTC mid marked at 07:00 GMT on 31 July — a London-morning mark, not a New York close, with no second-dealer corroboration and with CME CVOL unobtainable and the CBOE EVZ index discontinued since March 2025. The base-currency dossier's stale 3M implied of 5.70 (dated 13 May) is not used; 5.25 is used for all carry-to-vol denominators. The 1-year implied volatility percentile of approximately 20 is an estimate, not a computed distributional percentile.

Support and resistance: all support and resistance levels are web-sourced from technical analysis providers, as required — they cannot be derived from raw OHLC. Where providers disagree the range is presented rather than a point estimate. Fibonacci retracement anchors differ between providers and both are reported as cited rather than reconciled.

Forward points: forward points (+14.2/+42.2/+86.3 pips at 1M/3M/6M) are market-quoted values from the quote-currency dossier applied to current spot. The base-currency dossier's CIP-computed alternatives (+14.3/+37.5/+66.5) exclude cross-currency basis and are materially flatter at the back end. The 3-month EUR/USD cross-currency basis — the framework's designated benchmark for Factor 10 transmission — was not retrievable in either dossier; Factor 10 substitutes the SOFR-IORB spread, central bank liquidity swap usage and standing repo usage, and its confidence is held at 50/52 accordingly. Residual uncertainty in the 6-month outright is perhaps 5–10 pips against a stated 43-pip six-month edge.

Bilateral trade: bilateral goods trade figures (EUR exports to US $521.1bn, EUR imports from US $327.8bn, net EUR surplus $193.3bn, 2024) are taken directly from the injected IMF DOTS cache block without re-estimation. The mirror-image inconsistency (US-reported imports of $538.0bn versus EUR-reported exports of $521.1bn, a $16.9bn discrepancy) is typical of DOTS bilateral reconciliation; the euro-area-reported net figure of $193.3bn is used.

Positioning: CFTC figures use the 28 July report vintage (leveraged funds short 65,198 EUR contracts, asset managers long 209,326, open interest 819,806; ICE USD Index non-commercials +17,197, open interest 58,251), superseding the base dossier's own 21 July snapshot of -56,671. The 28 July reference date predates the 29–31 July breakout by three sessions, so the reported short is materially larger than the current position — that lag is treated as the stated tactical edge rather than corrected.

Weight adjustments: four adjustments were applied — tactical Factor 3 from 0.10 to 0.07 and Factor 5 from 0.06 to 0.09; strategic Factor 3 from 0.05 to 0.03 and Factor 1 from 0.24 to 0.26. Each is within the ±0.05 limit, each is offset within its own horizon, and both horizons sum to exactly 1.00.

Scoring: weighted scores are computed as stance score (Bullish +1, Neutral 0, Bearish -1) × confidence/100 × horizon weight, summed. Score-to-conviction bands: absolute score below 0.10 maps to Neutral; 0.10–0.25 to conviction 2; 0.25–0.45 to conviction 3; above 0.45 to conviction 4–5. The tactical score of +0.2302 sits at the top of the conviction-2 band and the strategic score of +0.1122 at the bottom; both placements are argued explicitly rather than mechanically applied.

Scenario probabilities: the 50/25/25 splits on both horizons are analyst judgements, not derived from an options-implied distribution, because no full volatility smile was obtainable for this pair this cycle. Expected spot levels (1.1620/1.1650/1.1680 at 1M/3M/6M) are likewise judgements.

Consensus reconciliation: bank forecasts are drawn from four separate aggregators that disagree materially. We quote all four ranges rather than reconciling them, and use 1.20 as the reference median for the divergence calculation because it is the more conservative of the two aggregate medians. Several aggregator pages carry stale internal detail (e.g., referencing an ECB deposit rate of 2.00%); their forecast levels are used but their rate narratives are not.

Interpretive choice on the standalone rankings: the most consequential judgement in this report is the decision to reach a marginally Bullish strategic conclusion despite the base dossier ranking EUR 6th of 11 and the quote dossier ranking USD 4th of 11 — a naive subtraction of which implies a bearish pair. The three bilateral grounds for departing from that subtraction (asymmetric energy netting, cancelling twin fiscal deteriorations, and the ECB's larger real-rate runway delivered at meetings preceding the FOMC) are stated in the G10 ranking section, and the resulting low conviction of 2 with a +3-pip expected value against the forward is the honest expression of how close that call is.
